central_topic: Minimal per-task targeted investment (L1 score boost or L0 number of tasks touched) needed for a target model to rank first on multi-task leaderboards under different aggregation rules, evaluated on Open LLM Leaderboard snapshots; post-draft gaps are comparator literature on priced/swap bribery under Copeland, Borda and plurality, the Open LLM Leaderboard as the held-out data source, and support for the leaderboard-incentive premise.
core_methods: Cost-minimizing bribery and manipulation analogues in computational social choice (priced, swap and weighted bribery)
Per-rule minimum-cost boost planners with verified plans (exact for mean/median/maximin/plurality; verified heuristics for trimmed mean/z-score/Borda/Copeland)
comparators: Priced, swap and weighted bribery in elections
Bribery and control complexity under Copeland, Borda and plurality, including score-based voting with per-voter costs
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard (v2) as the held-out data source (contents and results snapshots)
result_driven_themes: Incentives to optimize for leaderboard rankings (Goodhart's law, metric gaming in ML evaluation) as premise for the investment question

queries.query: priced bribery and swap bribery in elections computational complexity
queries.rationale: Targets the related-work paragraph 'Computational social choice' (anchor: 'Our problem is a continuous variant: the voters are tasks...'). The paper cites only generic bribery, manipulation and margin-of-victory works; cost-priced and swap bribery are the closest discrete analogues of the cost-per-task investment model, and reviewers will expect them. Distinct from existing entries (Faliszewski2006, Xia2012, Bartholdi1989), which are unpriced bribery, margin of victory and manipulation.

queries.query: bribery and control complexity for Copeland, Borda and plurality voting rules
queries.rationale: Same paragraph. Borda, plurality and Copeland are the rank-based rules the planner solves with heuristics or exact solvers; rule-specific bribery and control hardness results ground the claim that these rules need different solution methods. Existing citations address ties and few candidates, not these rules' bribery complexity. Include score-based and range voting with per-voter costs if returned.

queries.query: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 Hugging Face evaluation of open large language models
queries.rationale: Targets the related-work sentence 'The Open LLM Leaderboard aggregates six benchmarks' and the Data and splits paragraph. All held-out results use Open LLM Leaderboard snapshots, but only the six component benchmarks are cited, not the leaderboard itself. Resolve to the leaderboard description or evaluation-harness documentation; do not re-retrieve the component benchmarks or HELM, which are already cited.

queries.query: Goodhart's law metric gaming and leaderboard incentives in machine learning benchmarks
queries.rationale: Targets the introduction sentence 'Rankings influence adoption, publication and funding, so developers have an incentive to act on them', which is the stated premise of the study and has no support. One or two Goodhart or benchmark-culture references suffice. Avoid near-duplicates of Singh2025 (Leaderboard Illusion), Chen2026 (Leaderboard Incentives), Ethayarajh2020 and Dehghani2021, which are already in the bibliography.

forbidden_query_patterns: Any query naming or paraphrasing a withheld published paper on this exact research question (title, authors, results), or pages citing or discussing it
Generic: benchmarking, optimization, scientific method, paper writing
Chronology or search-history phrasing (cycles, attempts, incumbent scores)
Model-architecture queries (transformer, scaling); no architectures are trained
Titles already in references.bib (MMLU, BBH, HELM, Benchmark Lottery, Lanctot, Leaderboard Illusion, Zhou, Yang, Vote'n'Rank, Faliszewski, Xia, Bartholdi, Conitzer) except to resolve BibTeX
Software citations (NumPy, SciPy, MILP solver) and planner heuristics (bisection, greedy); deliberately not flagged by the gap artifact
